purpose: Supplement legible public-domain first-edition score evidence for Chopin Op.52 mm.191-203 and Op.61 m.24
Cross-check existing Op.60 m.24 and m.34 claims against the first edition and David Kopp paras.16-17 / Example 5 locator
Byte/source verification of the existing JSON and UConn PDF
prohibited_or_out_of_scope: No hold clearance, production cut, or boundary selection
No access to login credentials/cookies or circumvention of controls

evidence_labels.page_locator: CFEO catalog/pageview page and measure-span locator; establishes where a passage is, not an independent note reading.
evidence_labels.direct_score_read: Notation visibly inspected in the saved high-resolution public first-edition page image.
evidence_labels.commentary: Author or secondary prose; kept separate from first-edition notation claims.
evidence_labels.byte_source_check: File length and SHA-256 comparison only; no content interpretation.

bar_count_basis.method: The nineteenth-century score does not print continuous bar numbers. CFEO supplies each page span; count printed barlines sequentially from the page's first measure. P.11 contains 18 measures; m.191 begins after its first two 3-measure systems. P.12 first measure is m.203.
Count four measures in the first system; the first measure of the second system is m.24.
CFEO continuous page-span numbering; the first system of p.3 begins at m.24 and the first system of p.4 begins at m.34.

observations.bar_locator: mm.191-202, CFEO p.11; overall range locator, not every detail mapped to a unique bar
facts: Across the target page segment, upper-staff writing alternates chordal attacks with shorter slurred or beamed figures.
Lower-staff writing shows rapid grouped notes, low-register bass attacks, and broken-note motion.
Pedal marks, slurs/ties, and hairpin-shaped dynamic marks are visible.
observations.limit: This is a range-level notation description. It is not a bar-by-bar transcription, pitch transcription, or harmonic reduction.

observations.bar_locator: mm.191-202, CFEO p.11 later portion; exact single-bar placement not asserted
facts: The later portion of the target page span visibly prints the word stretto.
The closing portion visibly includes the dynamic marking fff.
observations.limit: These are printed score markings only; no affect or segmentation interpretation is made, and exact bar assignment is left open.

observations.bar_locator: m.203, CFEO p.12 first system, first measure
facts: The opening has longer-value chordal sonorities in both staves, ties/sustain, and a pedal mark.
observations.limit: No exact pitches, chord name, or functional-harmony claim is supplied.

observations.bar_locator: m.24, CFEO p.2 second system, first measure
facts: The upper staff begins with a rest, then enters with longer slurred notes.
The lower staff has more closely grouped moving notes, low-register noteheads, and a pedal mark.
The two staves visibly contrast a higher sustained/slurred line with a lower moving part.
observations.limit: No pitch transcription, harmonic function, or event/boundary interpretation.

observations.bar_locator: m.24, CFEO p.3 first system beginning
facts: A high-staff sustained sonority and printed trill continuation are visible with f.
The lower part has active broken-note/arpeggiated motion and pedal marks.
observations.limit: Score description only; the thematic/harmonic interpretation below is Kopp commentary.

observations.bar_locator: m.34, CFEO p.4 first system beginning
facts: The primary score visibly prints rallent.
observations.limit: Do not replace the printed rallent. with rit. The primary mark alone is not used to assert a beat-level onset.

commentary_checks.source: David Kopp, On Performing Chopin's Barcarolle, para.16
commentary_checks.commentary_claim: Kopp describes an extended A-sharp pedal in mm.20-22 and a direct return to F-sharp at m.24 after an A-sharp major triad.
commentary_checks.classification: Kopp's harmonic analysis; not a new reduction in this supplement.

commentary_checks.bar_locator: m.24 and following return span; Kopp Example 5 spans mm.23-35
commentary_checks.source: David Kopp, On Performing Chopin's Barcarolle, para.17 and Example 5
commentary_checks.commentary_claim: Kopp describes theme A / Rink A-prime as returning at m.24 with double trills, melodic diminution, and textural amplification.
commentary_checks.classification: Kopp's prose analysis; Example 5 heading/span checked only. Henle Urtext image not saved or copied.

commentary_checks.source: David Kopp, On Performing Chopin's Barcarolle, para.17
commentary_checks.commentary_claim: Kopp says inner-voice A-sharp 4 becomes A-natural at m.35.
commentary_checks.classification: Kopp commentary only; no new chromatic voice-leading reduction.

commentary_checks.commentary_claim: PTNA says the rallentando indication begins on beat 2.
commentary_checks.classification: Secondary commentary, not established from the primary score word alone.
